# 1 Chronicles Chapter 10 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 376r–376v

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa. **2** The Philistines pursued Saul and his sons closely, and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul. **3** The battle pressed hard against Saul, and the archers found him, and he was wounded by the archers.

**4** Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and deal shamefully with me." But his armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took his own sword and fell upon it. **5** When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died.

**6** So Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house died together. **7** When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled, and the Philistines came and settled in them.

**8** The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa. **9** They stripped him and took his head and his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to carry the news to their idols and to the people. **10** They put his armor in the temple of their gods and fastened his skull in the temple of Dagon.

**11** When all Jabesh-gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul, **12** all the valiant men arose and took away the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh and fasted seven days.

**13** So Saul died for his unfaithfulness which he committed against the LORD, against the word of the LORD which he did not keep, and also for consulting a medium to seek guidance. **14** He did not seek the LORD; therefore the LORD put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter is the Chronicler's prologue to the David narrative. By beginning with Saul's death rather than his reign, the Chronicler renders Saul as a negative theological example — a cautionary tale rather than a historical figure with complexity. The key term *ma'al* (unfaithfulness/sacrilege) in v.13 is the Chronicler's master concept: it will recur throughout his work to explain why kings and kingdoms fall. The chapter also introduces the Chronicler's principle of immediate divine retribution — sin produces consequences within the same narrative unit. The loyalty of Jabesh-gilead (vv.11-12) provides the only human warmth in an otherwise stark theological judgment.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.4 — "uncircumcised" vs. "pagans"
- **EMET:** "the-uncircumcised [arelim]"
- **LOGOS:** "these uncircumcised"
- **PNEUMA:** "these pagans"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "these uncircumcised" — *arelim* is a specific covenant-boundary term, not a general pejorative. PNEUMA's "pagans" loses the bodily/covenantal specificity.

### V.6 — "all his house" scope
- **EMET:** "and-all his-house — together they-died"
- **LOGOS:** "all his house died together"
- **PNEUMA:** "his entire dynasty came to an end"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "all his house died together" — PNEUMA's "dynasty came to an end" is interpretive commentary, accurate but beyond the Hebrew text.

### V.9 — messenger dispatch
- **EMET:** "and-sent into-the-land of-the-Pelishtim all-around to-bring-news [to] their-idols and-the-people"
- **LOGOS:** "sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to carry the news to their idols and to the people"
- **PNEUMA:** "sent word throughout Philistia, announcing the victory to their idols and their people"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS wording adopted. "Sent messengers" clarifies the implied verb; "carry the news" follows the Hebrew *levasseir*.

### V.13 — ma'al rendering
- **EMET:** "his-treachery [ma'alo] which he-committed-treachery [ma'al]"
- **LOGOS:** "his unfaithfulness which he committed"
- **PNEUMA:** "his unfaithfulness to the LORD"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his unfaithfulness which he committed against the LORD" — follows LOGOS with slight expansion for clarity. The cognate accusative (*ma'al ma'al*) is a Hebrew intensifier that cannot be fully replicated in English.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
